Robot Framework's syntax has a few rules that trip up newcomers, and all of
them are about **spacing and lines**:

- **Separation** — two or more spaces (or a tab) separate cells. A single space
  is part of the text.
- **Continuation** — `...` at the start of a line continues the previous line.
- **Comments** — `#` starts a comment to end of line.
- **Escaping** — `\` escapes a special character; `${SPACE}` is a deliberate
  single space.

This chapter's workspace has a broken suite at `checks/first_suite.robot`: its
cells are separated by a single space, so Robot Framework reads each line as one
long keyword name and cannot find it. Download this lesson's lab, then repair it.

> **Warning:** A single space does **not** separate cells. `Log Hello` is the
> keyword named "Log Hello", which does not exist — not the `Log` keyword with
> the argument "Hello".

## Task 1 — Fix the cell separation in the broken suite

Open `checks/first_suite.robot`. Each line uses single spaces. Widen the gap
between every keyword and its arguments to **two or more spaces**:

```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Greeting Reads Clean
    Log    Robot Framework is running
    Should Be Equal    apples    apples
```

**Check:** the suite now calls the `Log` and `Should Be Equal` keywords.

## Task 2 — Run the repaired suite green

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the test `Greeting Reads Clean` passes.
